newsitem.title: USA: LSB sees Q2 boosted by lower ammonia prices.
newsitem.headline: LSB sees Q2 boosted by lower ammonia prices.

text.p: LSB Industries Inc said Monday it expects a lower cost of ammonia in the second quarter to help second quarter results.
It said the price of its chemical business' primary raw material, anhydrous ammonia, averaged $45 more per ton in the first quarter 1997 as compared to the 1996 first quarter.
The cost of ammonia in the second quarter 1997 should average $40 per ton less than in the first quarter 1997, it said.
"This reduction, accompanied by higher sales volume due to seasonal demand, will favorably affect results in the second quarter," a company statement said.
Additionally, the company said it expects consolidation in the automotive parts industry should work in its favor.

"We are continuing to achieve reductions in the inventories of both our automotive and industrial products businesses with a $5.5 million reduction achieved in 1996 and an additional $7 million anticipated reduction in 1997," the company said.
The company attributed the loss to lower-than-expected margins in the chemical business and losses in its industrial and automotive products businesses.
